title: Choose the Org page structure
question: dia's look stays as it is; this picks how the Org page lays out roles, hired agents and the role editor.

options.label: Roles, then hired agents
options.thesis: One scrolling column: the retro warning, a Roles list, then a Hired agents list; Edit opens the role editor in a dialog.
options.viewport: Warning line, six role rows with switch and hire count, three hire rows with Rename, bypass override and Dismiss.
options.risk: Which agents belong to which role is read from a caption, not from position.

options.label: Role list and role detail
options.thesis: Roles on the left; the selected role's editor and its hired agents on the right, edited in place.
options.viewport: Role list with counts on the left, Strict engineer's fields and its one hire on the right.
options.risk: All hired agents are never visible at once; the page needs width the content area may not have beside the sidebar.

options.label: Roles and Hired agents tabs
options.thesis: Two tabs under the page header; each tab is one list, and the role editor opens in a dialog.
options.viewport: Retro warning above the tabs, the Roles tab open with six rows.
options.risk: Hiring from a role and then renaming the hire means switching tabs.

options.label: Midnight transit diagram
options.thesis: Roles as coloured lines with hires as stations.
options.viewport: A network diagram of roles and hires.
options.risk: Replaces dia's palette and a list's scanability with a diagram.
options.case: Loses on product clarity: an org of five roles is a list, not a network.
options.kept: Each role keeps one fixed position, so the list never reorders under the user.

options.label: Acetate tab manual
options.thesis: Each role as a coloured divider tab.
options.viewport: A stepped tab rail with a role per tab.
options.risk: Brings a new palette and type system DESIGN.md does not allow.
options.case: Loses on audience identification: a manual is not how dia presents settings.
options.kept: One size of row text does the work; hierarchy comes from weight.

options.label: Design annual plates
options.thesis: Roles as plates on a sheet.
options.risk: A print artifact on a working screen.
options.case: Loses on both axes: no task benefits from plates.
options.kept: Rows are divided by 1px hairlines, never boxed cards.

options.label: Event circle catalog
options.viewport: A dense grid of hire cells.
options.risk: Three hires do not fill a catalog grid.
options.case: Loses on product clarity at this data size.
options.kept: Dense rows: every role fits in the first viewport.

options.label: Labanotation score
options.thesis: Roles as columns on a staff.
options.viewport: A vertical staff of role columns.

options.label: Split-flap board
options.viewport: A board of hires with status columns.
options.risk: A costume of an instrument, which the Operate rules refuse.
options.kept: Columns never move; only values change.
